question.text: Ms. Ritu Kapoor, IC Chair at Godavari Cat III AIF, runs a MARKET-NEUTRAL long/short equity strategy using index options and delta-hedged pairs. The strategy is designed to be independent of broad market direction. Per Chapter 10, what is the MOST appropriate benchmark?

answer.text: NIFTY 50 TRI — since it is India's flagship broad-based index applicable to all Cat III AIFs regardless of strategy.

A FIXED pre-determined absolute-return hurdle (e.g., 10% p.a.) set by the Investment Manager at fund launch and disclosed in the PPM — absolute-return strategies are NOT benchmarked against broad-based relative indices.
S&P BSE Sensex price index — since the fund trades Indian equities, a price-only index is sufficient.
NIFTY IT Index — sectoral indices are the default benchmark for market-neutral strategies.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 10.8 explicitly: 'The benchmark for absolute-return strategies may be fixed rate, pre-determined by the Investment Manager at the time of launching the fund scheme, such as 10 percent per annum. Absolute Returns are NOT benchmarked against a broad-based market index or a relative benchmark.' Market-neutral, leveraged, and long/short concentrated positions fall in this category. The Trap: Option A applies a relative benchmark to a strategy designed to be market-independent — any positive market year would show 'underperformance' artificially. Options C and D are sectoral/price misfits. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B tests Cat III absolute-return basics for distributors. XIX-C tests the regulatory underpinning and PPM disclosure mechanics. Manager's Pro-Tip: Lock the absolute hurdle in the PPM at fund launch — changing it mid-tenure invites LP challenge. Also, internally track the fund against an overlay benchmark (e.g., Nifty 50 TRI) for IC reporting even though the external benchmark is the fixed hurdle — helps the IC diagnose whether alpha is truly market-neutral.
